chunks: And they denied them out of malice and pride, though in their hearts they believed that they were true. So see how was the end of evil-doers!

key_terms.ظُلْمًا: Malice or injustice, referring to denying the truth despite knowing it
key_terms.عُلُوًّا: Pride or arrogance, referring to haughtiness and superiority complex

ai.seo_question: Why did the disbelievers deny the truth despite believing in their hearts?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological state of the disbelievers, emphasizing that their rejection was an act of 'zulm' (consuming injustice) against their own souls, driven by 'uluww' (arrogant superiority). It underscores the distinction between intellectual conviction and practical acceptance, illustrating how pride blinds the heart to truth despite inner certainty. This serves as a warning that corruption stems not from ignorance, but from the willful distortion of known truth.
